plants.description: Replacing the per-member 'continue' with 'break' terminates the whole property loop, so every property after the first key-kind mismatch is silently dropped from the collected member list.
The ContainsKey guard is inverted: when the int key is already present the dictionary Add throws ArgumentException, and when it is absent the member is never registered at all.
The duplicate check for string-keyed properties now consults the int-key dictionary, so duplicate string keys are no longer detected and the subsequent Add throws ArgumentException.
For an int-keyed field, member.StringKey is null, so the guard calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(null) which throws ArgumentNullException and aborts analysis of the type.
Removes the registration of int-keyed properties into intMembers, so the analyzer no longer has the member/key mapping it needs and produces incomplete results.
Removes the registration of string-keyed properties into stringMembers, so those members are missing from the analyzer's collected member set.
Removes the registration of int-keyed fields into intMembers, so the analyzer no longer resolves the key mapping for those fields.
Removes the registration of string-keyed fields into stringMembers, leaving those members out of the collected member set the analyzer relies on.
Uses the indexer instead of Add; with the ContainsKey guard in place the behaviour is identical.
Uses the indexer instead of Add; with the ContainsKey guard in place the behaviour is identical.
Passes the same arguments by name; the call is unchanged.
Compares the ContainsKey result against false instead of negating it; logically identical.
